newsitem.title: USA: Epson asks court to reconsider patent ruling.
newsitem.headline: Epson asks court to reconsider patent ruling.

text.p: Epson America has asked a federal court to reconsider a ruling on printer cartridge patents in its legal dispute with Nu-kote Holdings Inc, a company official said Tuesday.

Epson's assistant general counsel said the company had asked the U.S. District Court for the Central District of California to reconsider its decision to declare the four patents "unenforceable." The ruling would prevent Epson, an affiliate of Seiko Corp, from imposing the patents on competitors to stop them from making cartridges for its ink-jet printers.
If the judge declines its request, Epson plans to bring its case to the Federal Circuit Court of Appeals in Washington, D.C., said the counsel, Alf Andersen.
"We're ready to appeal this," he said.
Epson is trying to prevent Nu-kote from making and selling cartridges that are compatible with its printers.

Angele Boyd, a printer industry analyst at International Data Corp, said the sale of these so-called after-market supplies can provide up to about 40 percent of the total revenues of printer makers like Epson.
"It's a huge business," she said. "The margins are higher on supplies (cartridges) than on hardware (printers).
"(And) they are going to try to stall third parties from getting in (the market) as long as possible," she added.
Nu-kote reported the court's decision earlier in the day, saying it lifted a preliminary injunction that prohibited it from selling its cartridges for the printers.
But Epson later said the injunction still stood.

On Tuesday, Nu-kote closed at 5-1/8 against a year low of five on the Nasdaq National Market, while Seiko closed at 700 yen in Tokyo. The ruling is part of a prolonged case involving other patents and trademark claims.
Nu-kote, which is embroiled in similar cases with Canon Inc and Hewlett-Packard Co, has also filed a counter claim for anti-trust against Epson.
In a statement released later in the day, Epson said the court held Nu-kote in contempt of court on March 10, ordering it to stop selling its cartridges for Epson printers.

"(It) also ordered Nu-kote to pay Epson the lost profits it would have earned on Nu-kote's...sales of cartridges in violation of the injunction," it said without saying how much the compensation might be worth.
Nu-kote officials were unavailable for comment on the release.
